incidents.vector: Zero-click Pegasus commercial spyware silently infected the target's phone via a malicious message, requiring no user interaction.
incidents.impact: Citizen Lab found the phone of former MEP Stelios Kouloglou was infected with Pegasus twice (Oct 2022, Mar 2023) while he sat on the parliamentary committee investigating spyware abuse; the same operator is tied to earlier hacks of Russian and Belarusian journalists.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — botnet / residential proxy operator
incidents.vector: Malicious SDKs bundled into smart-TV and streaming-box apps silently enrolled home devices as always-on residential proxy exit nodes rented to other criminals.
incidents.impact: FBI, IRS-CI, Google, Lumen and Shadowserver seized hundreds of domains tied to the NetNut proxy service (operated by Israeli firm Alarum Technologies) and the Popa botnet of 2M+ devices; Google observed 316 threat clusters using NetNut exit nodes in a single June week.

incidents.vector: Internet-wide password spraying plus exploitation of unpatched Fortinet, Sophos, Citrix VPN and MSSQL flaws, followed by a custom 'FortigateSniffer' that intercepted credentials on 24 protocols and offline GPU hash-cracking.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' campaign exposed valid admin/VPN credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate devices across government, telecom, finance, healthcare and critical infrastructure, including a Turkish NATO defense contractor from which classified documents were allegedly stolen; SOCRadar confirmed 12+ ransomware deployments (Inc, Lynx) stemming from the harvested access.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of critical Oracle E-Business Suite payments-processing flaw CVE-2026-46817 (CVSS 9.8), before any public proof-of-concept existed.
incidents.impact: Honeypots recorded six exploitation attempts from a single IP in a two-hour window, likely reconnaissance/weaponization testing; ~950 EBS instances remain internet-exposed (over half in the US), echoing last year's Clop mass-extortion of Oracle EBS victims.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 organizations (finance, HR, life sciences, public sector)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — phishing / business email compromise
incidents.vector: Phishing-as-a-service 'ARToken' panel (an EvilTokens affiliate) abuses Microsoft's OAuth device-code flow to steal tokens and Primary Refresh Tokens, bypassing MFA and surviving password resets.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos exposed a full BEC-as-a-service platform with 80+ API endpoints for token theft, mailbox access, SharePoint exfiltration and AI-assisted lures; observed lures spoofed a real vendor relationship to target an accounts-payable contact at a US life-sciences firm.

incidents.victim: Luxury jewelry retailer & US insurer (Scattered Spider breaches)
incidents.vector: Help-desk social engineering — attackers impersonated employees via phone/Google Voice to reset passwords and MFA, then used ngrok for persistent access.
incidents.impact: A 19-year-old alleged 'Scattered Spider' member (Peter Stokes) was extradited to the US over data-theft/extortion of a luxury-jewelry retailer (an $8M ransom demanded, ~$2M in losses) and a US insurer; the English-speaking crew is tied to 100+ intrusions and $100M+ in ransoms.

incidents.victim: Government officials, military, journalists & Ukraine-linked figures
incidents.vector: Phishing that impersonates commercial messaging-app support accounts to elicit victims' verification codes, PINs and, in an evolved tactic, Backup Recovery Keys.
incidents.impact: FBI and CISA updated their warning that Russian intelligence services continue an ongoing campaign against Signal/WhatsApp accounts of high-value targets; the US posted a $10M reward. Compromise of recovery keys allows takeover of historical messages and re-registered accounts.

incidents.victim: Amadey loader & StealC infostealer infrastructure (140,000+ PCs)
incidents.vector: Malware-as-a-service: Amadey served as an initial loader that deployed the StealC infostealer to harvest and resell credentials across underground markets.
incidents.impact: A Europol-led operation with seven law-enforcement agencies and six security firms seized 326 servers, 142 domains and $47M in crypto tied to the Amadey and StealC operations, which had infected 140,000+ computers and stolen 27M+ credentials; Amadey had also been used by Russian espionage actors against Ukraine.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government/military & entities tied to Italian foreign policy
incidents.vector: Deployment of a multi-component .NET backdoor ('STOCKSTAY') that masquerades as stock-market/PDF/calculator tools and communicates over encrypted WebSocket C2.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence detailed a new espionage backdoor used since 2022 by the Russia-linked Turla group (attributed by CISA to FSB Center 16); it supports file theft, screen capture, registry and command execution against government and military targets.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian governments & state-owned energy/water utilities
incidents.vector: Web-shell deployment on exposed web apps, followed by SoftEther VPN, Mimikatz, JuicyPotato and a new bespoke 'TinyRCT' backdoor with self-destruct/anti-analysis features.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Unit 42 detailed 10+ intrusions by Chinese-speaking cluster CL-STA-1062 (aka UAT-7237) against government entities and state-owned critical energy infrastructure in Southeast Asia, spanning full initial-access-to-exfiltration chains and lateral movement between agencies.

incidents.vector: Rogue peering and stolen certificate material for SSH access, then exploitation of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-day CVE-2026-20245 via a malicious CSV upload to gain root and create a hidden 'troot' account.
incidents.impact: Mandiant found a threat actor escalated to root on a service provider's SD-WAN Manager, exfiltrated fabric configurations, and used extensive anti-forensic cleanup; the campaign fits the 'living off the edge' pattern of state actors targeting network appliances for persistent access.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party firm managing the agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a wave of attacks on Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole the names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officials from the vendor that ran the agency's MDM platform, exposing sensitive personnel details of a national security service.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and mass document theft by the World Leaks data-extortion group, followed by public leaking after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a breach after World Leaks claimed 200,000+ stolen documents; leaked files reportedly include sensitive data on Apple and Tesla components and images of upcoming iPhone 18 batteries, chips and circuit boards.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion attributed to the ShinyHunters group, part of a broader extortion spree also tied to Oracle PeopleSoft exploitation.
incidents.impact: The US insurance sector's standards body was hacked and had to suspend insurer risk designations; some credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure while NAIC evicted the intruders and worked to restore operations.
